rule.help.required_activity: Compliant if the activity occurs. Absent in a complete case → violating; absent in an open case → not evaluable.
rule.help.forbidden_activity: Violating if the activity occurs at least once. Absent in an open case → not evaluable.
rule.help.precedence: Every occurrence of B needs an A with a strictly earlier timestamp. A tie with A → not evaluable. No B in a complete case → compliant (vacuous).
rule.help.max_duration: Completed throughput: only completed cases are judged. Observed duration: every case as recorded so far.
rule.help.max_occurrences: Violating when the activity occurs more often than allowed (repeats count). Open cases under the limit → not evaluable.
rule.help.start_activity: The first event must be one of the activities. Several events tied at the first timestamp with mixed activities → not evaluable.
rule.help.end_activity: Only complete cases are judged; the last event must be one of the activities.

algo.param.disable_fallthroughs: Disable fall-throughs: do not fall back to generic constructs (flower model, skips) when no cut is found.
algo.param.noise_threshold_im: Noise threshold (0–1): directly-follows relations less frequent than this share of an activity's most frequent outgoing relation are ignored when searching cuts.
algo.param.dependency_threshold: Dependency threshold (0–1): minimum dependency measure for an arc.
algo.param.and_threshold: AND threshold (0–1): minimum measure to treat two successors as parallel.
algo.param.min_act_count: Minimum number of occurrences for an activity to be kept.
algo.param.min_dfg_occurrences: Minimum number of occurrences for a directly-follows relation to be kept.
algo.param.powl_variant: POWL discovery variant (MAXIMAL, DYNAMIC_CLUSTERING, BRUTE_FORCE, TREE).
algo.param.order_graph_filtering_thresho: Order-graph filtering threshold (0.5 < x ≤ 1); only for the DYNAMIC_CLUSTERING variant.
algo.param.min_support_ratio: Minimum support ratio (0–1) of a constraint.
algo.param.min_confidence_ratio: Minimum confidence ratio (0–1) of a constraint.
algo.param.allowed_templates: DECLARE templates to discover (empty = all supported templates).
algo.param.noise_threshold_ls: Noise threshold (0–1) of the log skeleton.
algo.param.ts_direction: Direction of the state abstraction: forward (past events) or backward (future events).
algo.param.ts_window: Window size: number of events in a state.
algo.param.ts_view: State view: sequence, set or multiset of the windowed activities.
algo.param.seed: Random seed set by ProcessLens before calling the miner (the miner itself has no seed parameter).
algo.pre.nonempty: Needs at least one case in the selected population.
algo.pre.timestamps: Uses real event timestamps (durations between activities).
algo.lim.inductive: Guarantees a sound, perfectly fitting model; infrequent behaviour is kept, which can make the model imprecise (flower-like parts).
algo.lim.block_structured: Produces block-structured models only (process trees); some behaviour cannot be represented exactly.
algo.lim.imf: Infrequent behaviour below the noise threshold is dropped; fitness is no longer guaranteed.
algo.lim.imd: Works from the directly-follows graph only (scalable) and can lose information present in full traces.
algo.lim.heuristics: Heuristic, frequency-based model; soundness is not guaranteed. The Petri net is a derived representation used for replay.
algo.lim.heuristics_plusplus: ProcessLens passes atomic events (start = completion), so interval-based concurrency detection is not used.
algo.lim.alpha: Cannot discover short loops (length 1 and 2) or handle noise; the resulting net may be unsound.
algo.lim.alpha_plus: Extends Alpha with short-loop handling; still sensitive to noise and may yield unsound nets.
algo.lim.powl: POWL models express partial orders; the Petri net is derived for replay. Variant and filter settings change the model.
algo.lim.declare: Declarative constraints describe what must or must not happen; they do not give a single executable flow. Large logs can produce many constraints.
algo.lim.log_skeleton: Captures relations and frequency bounds observed in the log; it is not a process model and does not generalize beyond the observed behaviour.
algo.lim.transition_system: State abstraction depends on the window and view; there is no conformance method for transition systems here.
algo.lim.temporal_profile: Mean and standard deviation of times between activity pairs; assumes these times are roughly comparable across cases.
algo.lim.ilp: Region-based ILP discovery can be slow on large logs and produces nets without silent-transition structure guarantees.
algo.lim.genetic: Randomized search: results depend on the seed and parameters, runtime grows quickly with population and generations, and soundness is not guaranteed.

conf2.title: Formal conformance
conf2.intro: Check the selected cases against a discovered model or a user-approved reference model. Methods that do not apply, cannot be evaluated, fail or time out are shown as such — never as a score of zero.
conf2.population_note: Evaluated on the cases selected by the current global filters.
conf2.against_reference: Conformance to the approved reference model “{name}” (approved {date}).
conf2.against_discovered: Conformance to a model discovered by {name}; if it was discovered from the same cases, this measures how well the model describes its own training data.
ref.title: Reference models
ref.intro: A reference model is a model you explicitly approve (from a discovery run) or import as PNML/PTML. Conformance results state whether they were computed against a reference model or a discovered one.
cmp2.intro: Run several discovery algorithms on the same dataset version and filter snapshot and compare runtime, model size, fitness, precision and soundness. Metrics are shown side by side and are never combined into one overall score.
cmp2.split_enabled: Discover on training cases, evaluate on held-out cases
cmp2.split_note: Cases are assigned by a hash of the seed and the case ID, so the split is reproducible and a case's events are never divided between the two sets.
cmp2.held_out_note: Models were discovered on {train} training cases and evaluated on {test} held-out cases.
cmp2.in_sample_note: No split: models were discovered and evaluated on the same {n} cases (in-sample), which tends to overstate fitness.
cmp2.no_overall_score: Fitness and precision from token replay and from alignments are different measures; compare them only within the same column.
model.partial_order: Partial order (children without an order relation may run concurrently)
algo.oc_petri_net.name: Object-centric Petri net (OCPN)
algo.param.ocpn_variant: Inductive miner variant applied per object type: im (exact), imf (infrequent, uses noise_threshold), imd (directly-follows based).
algo.pre.ocel_nonempty: The selected object types must have at least one event-object relationship.
algo.lim.ocpn: Discovers one Petri net per object type by flattening internally and merges them on shared activities; variable arcs mark activities that usually involve several objects of a type. Interactions are not checked for soundness.
ocel.intro: Import OCEL 2.0 JSON logs where one event can relate to many objects of many types. Events are stored once; counts and costs never double-count shared events.
ocel.empty_hint: Upload an OCEL 2.0 JSON file or load the synthetic demo log.
ocel.supported_constructs: Supported: objectTypes, eventTypes, objects (typed attributes with time-stamped values, object-to-object relationships with qualifiers) and events (attributes, event-to-object relationships with qualifiers). Other keys are reported as warnings and not imported. XML and SQLite OCEL formats are not supported.
ocel.demo_description: Synthetic OCEL 2.0 log with customers, orders, items and packages. Packages can contain items of different orders, so many events are shared between objects.
ocel.confirm_delete: Delete “{name}” with all objects, relationships and runs?
ocel.filter_note: No selection means all types. Selecting types keeps events related to at least one object of a selected type; each event still counts once.
ocel.counting_note: Unique events count each event once even when it relates to several objects. Event-object relationships count each (event, object) link. Object transitions (in the OC-DFG) count consecutive event pairs per object.
ocel.cost_unique_sub: sum of the cost attribute, each event once
ocel.ocdfg_note: Nodes are event types (unique events). Edges are coloured by object type: an edge A → B of a type means an object of that type had event A directly followed by event B.
ocel.events_several_objects: Events with several objects of this type
ocel.pick_object: Choose an object to see its timeline, attribute history and related objects.
ocel.relations_note: Lifetime (first to last event) of objects of the selected type, grouped by how many related objects of another type they have. Descriptive only: an association, not a cause.
ocel.no_relations: No related objects of other types.
ocel.ocpn_note: Discovered with PM4Py's object-centric Petri net implementation on the selected object types. Places are coloured by object type; thick arcs are variable arcs.
ocel.ocpn_result: {places} places, {transitions} transitions, {variable} variable arcs · discovered in {s} s
ocel.variable_arc_legend: Thick arcs: variable (several objects per event)
ocel.projection_warning: Flattening picks one object type as the case notion. Events related to several objects of that type are copied into each object's case, events not related to the type are dropped, and relations to other types are lost. Event costs are not mapped to the cost field to avoid counting them several times.
ocel.projection_preview: {cases} cases, {rows} event rows from {unique} unique events.
ocel.projection_dup_warning: {dup} rows are copies of shared events. The new dataset keeps ocel_event_id and objects_sharing_event attributes so copies stay identifiable.
ocel.ack_flattening: I understand that flattening duplicates shared events and loses object relationships.
ocel.projection_description: Flattened from object-centric log “{name}” by object type {type}. {duplicated} event rows are copies of shared events ({unique} unique events). Relations to other object types are not included.
ocel.empty_selection: No events for the selected object types.
ocel.err.empty_selection: No events relate to the selected object types.
ocel.err.invalid: The OCEL file was rejected: {errors} errors (see details).
ocel.err.not_json_file: Only OCEL 2.0 JSON files (.json, .jsonocel) are supported.
ocel.finding.not_json: The file is not valid UTF-8 JSON: {detail}
ocel.finding.not_object: The top level must be a JSON object.
ocel.finding.unsupported_top_level: Top-level key “{key}” is not supported and was ignored.
ocel.finding.not_a_list: This section must be a list.
ocel.finding.attribute_without_name: Attribute without a name was ignored.
ocel.finding.unsupported_attribute_type: Attribute “{attribute}” has unsupported type “{type}”; stored as string.
ocel.finding.ignored_key: Key “{key}” is not supported and was ignored.
ocel.finding.duplicate_object_id: Object id “{id}” occurs more than once.
ocel.finding.undeclared_attribute: Attribute “{attribute}” is not declared for this type (kept as string).
ocel.finding.attribute_value_type: Value of “{attribute}” does not match declared type {type}.
ocel.finding.dangling_o2o: Object-object relationship points to unknown object “{target}”.
ocel.finding.dangling_e2o: Event-object relationship points to unknown object “{target}”.
ocel.finding.duplicate_event_id: Event id “{id}” occurs more than once.
ocel.finding.naive_times_utc: {count} event timestamps had no timezone offset and were read as UTC.
ocel.finding.no_events: The log contains no valid events.
ocel.finding.objects_without_events: {count} objects are not related to any event.
task.intro: Analyse exported user-interaction events (application + action) by session: task variants, repeated sequences, application switches and links to business cases. ProcessLens does not record screens or keystrokes.
task.empty_hint: Import a task-event CSV or load the synthetic demo.
task.privacy_note: Only the mapped fields are stored; all other columns are dropped and listed. User ids must be pseudonymous (values containing “@” are rejected).
task.demo_description: Synthetic interaction events of clerks posting invoices of the purchase-to-pay demo (e-mail, PDF viewer, ERP, spreadsheet). Linked to the demo dataset when it is loaded.
task.mode.source_and_inactivity: Exported session id, split at inactivity
task.session_note: Events are ordered by user, timestamp and source row. With the inactivity rule a new session starts when the user changes or the gap to the previous event exceeds the threshold.
task.time_note: Working time is never inferred. Elapsed span is the time between a session's first and last event; durations come only from the exported duration column, with their coverage shown.
task.elapsed_sub: first to last event, not working time
task.sequences_note: Contiguous sequences of steps within sessions. A sequence is hidden when a longer one covers exactly the same occurrences.
task.no_sequences: No sequence repeats across the required number of sessions.
task.switch_summary: {switches} of {transitions} consecutive steps switch application ({share}). {sessions} of {total} sessions contain a switch; median {median} switches per session.
task.dfg_frequency_only: Edges show how often one step directly followed another within a session. Node durations come only from explicitly exported durations.
task.cases_summary: {cases} business cases; {linked} events carry a case id, {unlinked} do not.
task.not_linked_hint: Link a dataset to check which cases exist and open them.
task.err.encoding: The file is neither UTF-8 nor Windows-1252 text.
task.err.unreadable: The CSV could not be read: {detail}
task.err.duplicate_columns: The CSV has duplicate column names.
task.err.column_twice: A column is mapped to more than one field.
task.err.no_rows: The file has no data rows.
task.err.invalid_rows: Import rejected: {invalid} of {total} rows are invalid (see details).
task.err.mapping_json: The mapping must be a JSON object.
task.err.length_range: The maximum length must not be smaller than the minimum length.
task.finding.invalid_duration: Invalid duration “{value}” (must be a non-negative number of seconds).
task.finding.user_id_not_pseudonymous: {count} user ids look like e-mail addresses. Pseudonymize user ids before importing.
task.finding.session_several_users: {count} exported sessions contain events of several users.
task.finding.rows_without_session: {count} events have no session id; they are grouped by the inactivity rule.
